title: Three perfect days in Los Angeles, from Exposition Park to the Pacific
dek: George Lucas's new museum, Brahms at Disney Hall with the LA Phil's next music director, a long warm Saturday on the Westside and the Fugees' The Score at the Hollywood Bowl.

hero.caption: The Santa Monica Pier, where Saturday's walk along the sand ends just before the sun goes down.

intro:
The clocks went back last Sunday, the Halloween decorations are down, and Los Angeles has slipped into the part of autumn that visitors rarely expect: the forecast for this weekend is dry and warm, with highs in the low to mid 80s and the sun setting just before 5 p.m. That makes for short, golden afternoons, so this plan puts the beach on Saturday and keeps the evenings for music.

The big new thing in town is the **Lucas Museum of Narrative Art**, which opened in Exposition Park on September 22 with more than 1,200 works across about 30 galleries, from *Star Wars* production designs and costumes to Norman Rockwell, Jack Kirby and Dorothea Lange. Next door, the California African American Museum has a show built around the juke-joint music of the film *Sinners*. On Friday night **Daniel Harding**, the Los Angeles Philharmonic's music director designate, conducts Bernstein's "Jeremiah" Symphony and Brahms' Second Piano Concerto with Leif Ove Andsnes at Walt Disney Concert Hall, repeated Saturday night and Sunday afternoon.

Sunday is busy across the basin: the Chargers host the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium at 1:05 p.m., the Clippers play the Pelicans at Intuit Dome in the evening, and **Ms. Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean** mark 30 years of the Fugees' *The Score* at the Hollywood Bowl.

The three days each stay in one corner of the city. Friday runs from downtown to Exposition Park and back for the concert. Saturday is the Westside: the Getty Center in the morning, then Santa Monica and the sand. Sunday goes east to Pasadena and San Marino for the Huntington's gardens and the Norton Simon's paintings, before ending under the stars in the Cahuenga Pass.

days.title: Friday: downtown and Exposition Park
days.intro: A new museum and an old food hall by day, then a French brasserie and the LA Phil at Disney Hall by night.

stops.name: Grand Central Market
stops.text: Downtown's food hall has fed Angelenos since 1917, and it is at its calmest on a weekday morning, before the lunch crowd from the office towers arrives. Walk the length of the arcade from Broadway to Hill Street, pick up coffee and a breakfast sandwich, and sit at one of the shared counters to watch the stalls open. The market opens at 8 a.m. daily, but individual vendors set their own hours. From here the Metro E Line runs south to Exposition Park.

stops.name: Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
stops.text: George Lucas's museum of storytelling in pictures opened in September, and its first installation fills about 30 galleries with more than 1,200 works. Production designs, props and costumes from the Lucas Archives sit alongside Norman Rockwell, N.C. Wyeth, Beatrix Potter, Jack Kirby, Dorothea Lange and Alison Bechdel, so a comic page and an illustration from a century ago end up in conversation. Adult tickets are $25 and anyone 17 and under gets in free. Book a timed entry ahead; on Fridays the museum is open until 9 p.m. and it is closed on Tuesdays.

stops.name: Holbox
stops.addr: Mercado La Paloma, 3655 S Grand Ave
stops.text: A short walk east of the park, inside the Mercado La Paloma food hall, Gilberto Cetina's seafood counter holds a Michelin star and a place on North America's 50 Best Restaurants list. Order the smoked kanpachi taco on an heirloom tortilla with Oaxacan cheese and salsa macha, then whatever raw seafood is on the board that day. At lunch it is counter service, à la carte; the tasting menu is only on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Holbox serves no alcohol.

stops.name: California African American Museum
stops.text: Free and rarely crowded, CAAM has one of the shows of the fall: *Sinners: Sounds That Summon*, organized around the film's Club Juke sequence. You will find the original Club Juke sign, Smoke and Stack's costumes and Sammie "Preacher Boy" Moore's guitar, set in the history of the Great Migration, and it ends with a room where visitors can record their own musical memories. The museum is open until 5 p.m.; Exposition Park parking is $20, or $24 after 5 p.m.

stops.name: Kendall's Brasserie
stops.text: Take the train back downtown for an early dinner beneath the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion, two minutes' walk from Disney Hall. This is a classic French brasserie with a raw bar, and the order is steak frites or the branzino, with an onion soup gratinée to start. It is open from 5 to 8 p.m. on Fridays, so an early table fits an 8 p.m. concert; tell your server when you sit down. Book ahead.

stops.name: LA Phil at Walt Disney Concert Hall
stops.text: Daniel Harding, named the LA Phil's next music director this spring, conducts Bernstein's Symphony No. 1, "Jeremiah," with mezzo-soprano Avery Amereau, and Brahms' Second Piano Concerto with Leif Ove Andsnes. The concert runs about an hour and a half with no intermission. Friday is a Casual Friday: afterward Harding talks with the orchestra's chief executive, Kim Noltemy, and there is a free beer or cider tasting. Tickets start at $20; a free preconcert talk begins at 7 p.m.

days.title: Saturday: the Getty and the Santa Monica shore
days.intro: Art on a hilltop in the morning, the beach in the warm afternoon, and dinner and a dance floor on Main Street.

stops.name: Huckleberry Cafe
stops.text: A cozy bakery and cafe on Wilshire with wooden tables and vintage chairs, good for a slow start before a long day. The signature Huckleberry Breakfast is the full plate; Green Eggs & Ham is made with Niman Ranch ham, and the breakfast burrito is the quick option if you want to be at the Getty when it opens. Saturday mornings are busy, so come early.

stops.name: Getty Center
stops.text: Ride the tram up from the parking garage to the hilltop campus above the 405, where the collection runs from European paintings to photography, and the terraces look across the whole basin to the ocean. Admission is free but needs a timed reservation. On Saturdays the Getty stays open until 9 p.m., the latest of the week. Parking is $25 per car, cashless, and drops to $15 after 3 p.m. It is closed on Mondays.

stops.name: Bay Cities Italian Deli
stops.text: Back down the hill, this Italian deli and bakery has been a Santa Monica fixture for generations, and its Godmother is the sandwich locals call the best in town: prosciutto, ham, capicola, mortadella, Genoa salami and provolone on a crusty roll. Ask for it "with The Works," which adds peppers, hot or mild, and dressing. The line on a Saturday is long; order online ahead and walk straight to the pickup counter. Take it to the beach.

stops.name: Santa Monica Pier and the beach path
stops.text: With highs forecast in the 80s, this is the afternoon to be by the ocean. Walk out along the pier past the Ferris wheel to the end for the view back up the coast to Malibu, then follow the path south along the sand toward Ocean Park, or rent a bike. Sunset is at about 4:54 p.m., so be back near the water for it; the light on the pier is at its best in the half hour before. Afterward, walk inland a few blocks to Main Street for dinner.

stops.name: Chinois on Main
stops.text: Wolfgang Puck opened this room in 1983, and it still pairs Asian flavors with California ingredients. It still looks the part, with a fish tank and a festive room. Start with the Chinese chicken salad and the Shanghai lobster, then share the sizzling whole catfish in ponzu. It is a splurge; book ahead for Saturday.

stops.name: Circle Bar
stops.text: Two blocks south, the oval bar that opened in 1949 and once drew Jim Morrison and Truman Capote has reopened under Mark and Addie Van Gessel, who also run Venice's Hinano Cafe, after nearly three years closed. The floor plan and the old sign survive; now there is a bigger dance floor, a DJ booth called the Halo and a good sound system. Order the Pacific Cooler. It is open Thursday to Saturday, 6 p.m. to 2 a.m.

days.title: Sunday: Pasadena, San Marino and the Hollywood Bowl
days.intro: Gardens and old masters in the San Gabriel Valley, then the Fugees' greatest album under the stars.

stops.name: Marston's
stops.text: A Pasadena breakfast favorite on Walnut Street, a few blocks north of Old Pasadena. Order the French toast or the avocado toast with heirloom tomatoes. It opens at 8 a.m. on weekends and serves until 2:30 p.m.; Sunday mornings are busy, so arrive near opening. Then drive south to San Marino for the Huntington.

stops.name: The Huntington
stops.text: Henry Huntington's estate is a library, an art museum and botanical gardens on one ticket. See Gainsborough's *The Blue Boy* in the main house, then spend most of the morning outdoors: the desert garden, the Japanese garden and the Chinese Garden of Flowing Fragrance. Weekend visits need advance tickets, which run about $29 to $34 for adults; parking is free. It is open 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and closed on Tuesdays.

stops.name: Lunasia
stops.text: Back in Pasadena, Lunasia serves dim sum all day on weekends, so there is no rush to beat a cart. Order har gow, char siu bao and turnip cake, and finish with the egg tarts. On weekends it is open from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. It is a short drive west along Colorado Boulevard to the Norton Simon.

stops.name: Norton Simon Museum
stops.text: Norton Simon's collection hangs in quiet galleries on Colorado Boulevard, and on a Sunday afternoon it is rarely crowded. Give most of your time to the European paintings, then step out into the sculpture garden. Admission is $20 for adults and free for anyone 18 and under and students. It is open noon to 5 p.m. on Sundays and closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, so this is the weekend's window.

stops.name: Agnes Restaurant & Cheesery
stops.text: Vanessa Tilaka and Thomas Kalb's restaurant fills a former fire department horse stable, with a cheese counter at one end and a hearth at the other. Have the cornbread eclair filled with chicken liver mousse and topped with Luxardo cherries, a cheese and charcuterie board, and Kalb's radiatori in tomato sauce. On Sundays it closes at 8 p.m., so an early dinner leaves time to drive to the Bowl. Book ahead.

stops.name: Ms. Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean at the Hollywood Bowl
stops.text: Thirty years after the Fugees released *The Score*, Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean bring the album to the amphitheater in the hills. Expect "Killing Me Softly," "Ready or Not" and "Fu-Gee-La." Bring a layer: it will be warm at sunset, but nights in the hills cool down. Leave plenty of time to get there, because Sunday traffic is heavy.

stay.name: Shutters on the Beach
stay.text: A hotel on the sand that calls itself a Cape Cod beach house on the Pacific, with ocean-view rooms, One Spa, and 1 Pico and Coast for dinner by the water. With warm, dry weather forecast, it puts Saturday's beach walk and Main Street on your doorstep, and the Getty is a short drive up the 405.

stay.name: Millennium Biltmore Hotel
stay.text: Downtown's grand old hotel faces Pershing Square, a three-minute walk from the Metro, with the Gallery Bar and Cognac Room for a martini. It suits Friday best: Grand Central Market, Disney Hall and the train to Exposition Park are all close.

stay.name: The Hoxton, Downtown LA
stay.text: A 174-room hotel in the restored 1922 Los Angeles Railway building on Broadway, with a rooftop pool and bar over the old theater district. It is close to the Metro for Exposition Park and Union Station's FlyAway bus to LAX.

events.name: Daniel Harding Leads Bernstein & Brahms
events.when: Fri. and Sat. 8 p.m., Sun. 2 p.m.
events.text: The LA Phil's music director designate conducts Bernstein's "Jeremiah" Symphony and Brahms' Second Piano Concerto with Leif Ove Andsnes. Tickets from $20; free preconcert talk an hour before.

events.name: Alanis Morissette: Butterfly With a Machete residency
events.text: Alanis Morissette's Los Angeles residency plays the YouTube Theater at Hollywood Park through the middle of next week.

events.name: LA Kings vs. Pittsburgh Penguins
events.text: The Kings host the Pittsburgh Penguins downtown on Saturday evening.

events.name: Competing Cosmologies: Interpreting the Sky
events.text: The Wende Museum opens a new exhibition, *Competing Cosmologies: Interpreting the Sky*, on Saturday. The opening is free.

events.name: Los Angeles Chargers vs. Houston Texans
events.text: The Chargers host the Texans in Week 9, televised on CBS. Expect heavy traffic around Inglewood and LAX through the afternoon.

events.name: Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean: Celebrating 30 Years of The Score
events.text: The two Fugees reunite to play their 1996 album at the Bowl.

events.name: Los Angeles Clippers vs. New Orleans Pelicans
events.text: The Clippers' Sunday evening game follows the Chargers game a few blocks away, so Inglewood stays busy all day.

know: **From LAX.** Take the free shuttle from the terminals to the LAX/Metro Transit Center, then the K Line or C Line into the rail network; a ride is $1.75, with free transfers for two hours when you tap a TAP card, a contactless bank card or a phone. The FlyAway bus runs nonstop between the terminals and Union Station downtown. From Burbank, Long Beach, Orange County or Ontario, a taxi or rideshare is usually simplest.

**Getting around.** You will want a car or rideshare for Saturday and Sunday. The Metro E Line links downtown (7th St/Metro Center and Pershing Square are close to the hotels) with Exposition Park and Santa Monica, which makes Friday easy without a car.

**Parking.** Exposition Park lots charge $20 a day, or $24 if you arrive after 5 p.m. The Getty charges $25 a car, $15 after 3 p.m. and nothing after 6 p.m. on Saturdays. The Huntington's lot is free.

**Closed days.** The Getty is closed Mondays; the Huntington and the Lucas Museum close on Tuesdays, and the Norton Simon on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. If you stay into Veterans Day week, plan around those days.

**Sunday traffic.** The Chargers play at SoFi Stadium at 1:05 p.m. and the Clippers at Intuit Dome at 6 p.m., both in Inglewood near LAX, and the Hollywood Bowl concert is at 7:30 p.m. Allow extra time on the 405 and the 101, and for any Sunday trip to the airport.

**The weather and the light.** The forecast is dry and unusually warm, with highs in the low to mid 80s Fahrenheit and lows in the upper 60s. Daylight saving time ended last Sunday, so the sun sets at about 4:55 p.m. Bring sunscreen and a light layer for the evening.
**Tipping.** Tip at sit-down restaurants and bars as you would elsewhere in the United States, and check the bill first, since some Los Angeles restaurants add a service charge.
